source.title: A Model Zoo on Phase Transitions in Neural Networks
source.authors: Konstantin Schürholt; Léo Meynent; Ye-Fan Zhou; Haiquan Lu; Yao-Qing Yang; Damian Borth

record.tranche_reason: The study reports training accuracy across CIFAR model zoos, bearing on whether the trained networks fit their training sets. It does not reproduce the specific corrupted-label or random-label experiments in V1.
record.gate_note: The reported training-accuracy distributions in Table 7 are rows. The paper also describes loss landscapes and downstream methods, but those results do not measure training classification error for the versions listed.
record.test_reason: The study's own randomly initialized ResNets are trained with SGD on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 and evaluated by training classification accuracy, directly testing the clean-label fitting component of V1.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors conclude that their structured, phase-annotated model zoos cover known phases across architectures and domains, and that phase-dependent outcomes extend to downstream methods. They report that low-training-loss regions exceed high-test-performance regions and describe performance as competitive for model size, while emphasizing that the zoos prioritize phase diversity.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains ResNet and ViT model zoos with Kaiming Uniform initialization and fixed optimizer recipes while varying width and batch size. ResNets use SGD and ViTs use AdamW. It does not report corrupted-label experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The study varies model width and batch size across its zoos; train-accuracy distributions vary by architecture and dataset. The reported table does not identify which settings produced each range endpoint.

fits_no_version.finding: ViT training accuracy averages 0.71 on CIFAR-10 and 0.37 on CIFAR-100, with maxima of 1.00 and 0.88 respectively.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Transformer fitting performance varies substantially across width, batch-size, and dataset recipes.

record.problems: Table 7 aggregates over each model zoo, so it does not associate train-accuracy values with specific widths or other settings. Corrupted or random labels are not tested. Train accuracy is reported, not classification error directly.
record.rows_left_out: No additional training-accuracy results matching V1 were omitted. Figure-only phase plots and results on non-CIFAR datasets were not extracted because Table 7 gives the relevant CIFAR training-accuracy distributions.

untested.parts: Corrupted and random labels; which widths and batch sizes attain near-zero error; effects of training duration, early stopping, or regularization. Training accuracy does directly determine classification error as one minus accuracy.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student optimization, spurious-minimum frequencies, and the benefit of one or two extra student neurons.
Controlled depth comparisons with and without identity shortcuts, longer training, and special initialization alternatives.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, signal or gradient propagation, training speed, and maximum trainable depth.

Learning-rate stability thresholds, transient loss growth and curvature reduction, edge-of-stability trajectories, and divergence relative to the threshold. Section 5.1 discusses prior work rather than testing these.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without batch normalization, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The aggregate rows are partial because they combine near-perfect and poor fitting. Their low endpoints do not establish a failure of sufficiently large networks: Table 7 does not identify the corresponding widths or batch sizes, and V1 already allows substantial error in smaller or restricted recipes. Consequently, these distributions alone warrant neither a challenges verdict nor an additional scope restriction.

versions.untested_parts: Corrupted or random labels, explicit error-rate results, and a mapping of training error to model size and training duration are not reported.
